correctness.rationale: Under unitary monodromy, L² holomorphic Laurent coefficients extend across lattice punctures and are bounded entire functions, so only indices k with ak integer survive. Irrational a leaves the constant nonvanishing canonical form; rational p/q leaves k multiples of q, giving annulus Laurent series F_q(S) with I_0=log 2 and I_k=(2^{2k}-1)/(2k). Classical annulus scalar-kernel zero theorem provides exactly two simple negative-real zeros. Inversion F_q(S)=F_q(4^q/S) and the nonzero derivative of eta↦eta^q produce 2q simple scalar fibres (not fixed-basepoint zero counts). Set S=qy: the negative Laurent tail is 2/y+4/(q y²)+O(q^-2) and positive tail O(q²4^-q), uniformly near y=-2log2, yielding the simple zero y=-2log2+2/q+O(q^-2). Numerical 69-term series roots at q=6,10,20,40,80 corroborate exact expansion; these truncated roots are not an infinite-series certificate.

value.rationale: A sharp boundary-collar location and explicit second-order product-root asymptotic for finite-holonomy Bergman zero fibres extends a qualitative two-zero theorem into a quantitative degeneration law on a natural pseudoconvex bundle family. The claimed statistic is a motivated geometric locus, not an arbitrary finite example.

final_claim: Irrational holonomy gives zero-free canonical Bergman kernel; rational holonomy p/q gives exactly two q-fold simple scalar product-zero circles and S_{q,-}=-2q log 2+2+O(1/q), with sharp q log(r_minus)-log q -> log(2 log 2) and symmetric outer circle.
limitations: Two q-fold circles mean scalar product-value fibres, not cardinality of zeros at a fixed second argument.
Finite 69-term numerical Laurent evaluations are diagnostics; uniform tail expansion and classical two-root theorem establish the claim.
